cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is writing to the believers in Corinth. He tells them about the time he went to Troas to preach the gospel of Christ. And when he got there, a door stood open for him in the Lord.
A wide-open door to preach, friend! Paul should be doing a happy dance. Instead, he says he had no peace in his spirit.

cards.question: Paul had no peace in his spirit in Troas because he didn't find his brother ___ there.
No Titus in Troas, and no peace for Paul. So what does Paul do, even with that open door?

answers.text: Says goodbye and goes on to Macedonia
Stays in Troas and keeps on preaching
Sails straight back across to Corinth

cards.text: Talk about a turn. One line Paul's leaving Troas with no peace, and the next it's "But thanks be to God," who always leads them triumphantly as captives in Christ.

cards.question: Paul says God always leads him and his team triumphantly in Christ. What does God spread everywhere through them?

answers.text: The sound of His great name
The light of His holy law

cards.text: Friend, I open ONE oven door and the whole Dorinverse knows what's baking. Paul says that to God, he and his team are the sweet aroma of Christ.

cards.question: Paul says he and his team are the sweet aroma of Christ only among those who are being saved.
Same aroma of Christ, two very different results. Paul says that to one group they're an odor that brings ___, and to the other a fragrance that brings ___.

cards.text: Then Paul asks, "And who is qualified for such a task?" Friend, if you'd asked me that back in the junk drawer with my blurry edges, I'd have pointed my mustache at myself and said NOT THIS GUY.

cards.question: Paul says he and his team are just like so many others, who peddle the word of God for profit.

cards.text: No infomercial here. No "but WAIT, there's more." In Christ, Paul says, they speak before God with sincerity, as men sent from God.
Then Paul asks if they're commending themselves again, or if they need letters of recommendation, like some people do. That's like handing your boss a résumé after ten years on the job.

cards.question: Forget letters of recommendation. Who does Paul tell the church in Corinth is his letter?
Paul says the Corinthians are a letter from Christ, and it isn't written with ink. So what is this letter written with?

answers.text: The Spirit of the living God
The blood of the faithful prophets
The oil used to anoint kings

cards.question: This letter from Christ isn't written on tablets of stone. Paul says it's written on tablets of human ___.

cards.text: Paul says confidence like that before God is theirs through Christ. Not through anybody's résumé.

cards.question: Paul says their competence comes from God, not from themselves.
Remember Paul asking who is qualified? That word again. Paul says God has qualified them as ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the ___.
Paul says the letter kills. What does he say the Spirit does?

findings.problem: The card says Paul is writing to the believers in Corinth. That fact comes from outside the passage (2 Corinthians 1:1), but the card gives no reference for it and cites only 2 Corinthians 2:12.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "A wide-open door" stretches the text. Verse 12 says only that "a door stood open," and this line is narration, not one of Papa Dorin's own jokes.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Card 5 gives nothing that points toward fragrance or smell, so picking "The fragrance of knowing Him" over "The light of His holy law" or "The sound of His great name" is luck. Card 7's oven-door aroma line would set this up, but it comes after the question.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The question says only "to one group" and "to the other," and no card before it names the two groups (being saved and perishing). A baker who puts "life" in blank 1 and "death" in blank 2 could argue they're right. The question also doesn't say which group is which.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
